The unused opcodes ($01, $3A, $3D, $3E, $45, $46, $6E, $70, $74, $78, $79, $85, $86, $93, $9B, $A2–$A5, $BE, $BF, $C5, $C6, $DB, $E9, $EF, $F5–$F7, $FB–$FD) all point at Evt_UnusedOpcode ($C0:5F6E), which stops the game on the colour Halt_ColorBadOpcode.

Operands follow common conventions: "slot" is an object × 2; "p" is 0, 2 or 4 for a party member; "a"/"b" name event words at Evt_Unk7F0200 + a × 2 (a byte stored into one goes to its low byte only); "m" is an address in bank $7F (Evt_Mem7F + m); "ptr" is a 3-byte long address. Jump distances are unsigned bytes counted from the operand itself, forward for every jump but $11. A condition opcode goes on with the next opcode when its condition holds and jumps when it does not.

docs.title: Movement
docs.text: The movement opcodes set up a timed move and then return their own position with C=0 until it is done, keeping Obj_Unk1A80 nonzero meanwhile. They lean on the object motion code: Obj_CalcDirection ($C0:ABA2, an angle with 256 steps per turn from a 32×32 table), Obj_SetVelocity and Obj_SetVelocityChecked (steps from the angle and speed with the hardware multiplier), and Obj_MoveStep / Obj_MoveStepFree, which the per-frame object pass Vblank_UnkA810 runs. Evt_Op7A_ArcToTile moves an object along an arc to a tile ("probably a jump", per its header), with a gravity operand.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
The message opcodes ($B8, $BB, $C0–$C4) wait until Field_Unk29 is 0, start Field_Unk1F87's sequence with a number, the object and a pointer set by Evt_OpB8_SetMsgPtr, then wait for it to finish. A treasure (Field_CheckTileInFront) starts the same sequence.

Field_Unk1F87 ($C0:1F87, run every frame from GameLoop_FrameBody) is the message window's frame step; its banner suggests the name Field_MessageStep. It works by state in Field_Unk29: clear the 1 KB text buffer at $7E:F000 (Field_MsgClearBuf) and let the NMI send it to the four text lines; open the window a step a frame, placing it in the upper or lower half of the screen ("away from the object, probably") unless Field_Unk30 fixes the place; draw the text one glyph a step with bank $C2's text window (TextWin_Init / TextWin_Step, through Field_MsgStart and Field_MsgStep); wait; then close the window step by step. The status codes the string's control codes set (TextWin_Status) drive the waits: the end, a timed wait (its argument × 15 frames), a new line or a new page, some after a button press. A choice cursor (Field_Unk62, 64, 65) runs in the wait state, "probably". The text-line reading of Field_Unk31, and the reading of the status codes, come from what the code does with them.

docs.title: Items, gold and characters
docs.text: The item and gold opcodes ($C7, $C9–$CE) call the bank-$C1 services behind BankC1_Entry8003 (BankC1_ServiceTable, $C1:D126): 0 finds an item in the inventory, 1 adds one, 2 removes one, 3 tests the 24-bit gold against an amount, 4 adds gold, 5 takes it off when there is that much. The character opcodes ($CF–$D3), the item count ($D7) and $D5, $F8–$FA go through BankC2_Entry8004 to the menu's command handler Menu_Unk8C36 (not matched); its character commands work on the 9-byte list Menu_PartyOrder (three party places, then six reserve places).

docs.title: Party walks
docs.text: Evt_OpD9_PartyWalkToTiles walks the leader and the two other members to three tiles, and Evt_OpDA_PartyGather walks members 2 and 3 to the leader. Both send the members off on small scripts that LocLoad_InitUnk7F3700 seeds at $7F:3700 (each member runs at level 0) and wait in the calling object until every member is back.

docs.title: Quirks kept
docs.text: The handlers keep the original's oddities, each documented in its header. A few: Evt_Op00_Return's level search has no upper bound; Evt_Op6F_ShrVarByte treats a count of 0 as 256 shifts; the comparison numbers of opcodes $12–$16 and the bit numbers of $63–$66 are not masked; Evt_OpB6_FollowPc is missing a CLC; Evt_InitObjects fills three bank-$7F tables and then clears them again in its next step.

docs.title: What is not matched yet
docs.text:
Every opcode handler is matched. Outside the interpreter, the code the handlers lean on that is not matched yet:

  • Where $FF with a second byte below $90 goes: bank $C3 (BankC3_Entry0000) and the bank-$FD vectors FdVec_FFF1, FdVec_FFEB, FdVec_FFE8, FdVec_FFE5. These leave the field for good.
  • The menu's command handler Menu_Unk8C36, behind the character opcodes.
  • FdVec_FFF7's routine (EngFD_UnkE39C), which works each frame on the palette-animation records that $2E and $88 fill.

docs.title: Frame cycle and NMI
docs.text:
How one frame of the field runs: the game logic in GameLoop_FrameBody, the end-of-frame work that prepares the next picture, the frame wait, and the NMI handler that uploads it during vertical blank. The scene mode in bank $C2 and the battle have frame cycles of their own, summarised at the end.

See also: Engine core, Boot, Architecture.

docs.title: One field frame
docs.text:
GameLoop_FrameBody ($C0:0097)
  input, scene changes, field update, event hooks …   game logic (see Engine core)
  Field_EndOfFrame ($C0:00BF)
    Vblank_Unk59D9               queue the objects whose script timer ran out
    Vblank_ReadScanlineCounters  run their scripts while the frame has time
    JSL EngFD_UnkC2C1            one HDMA table builder (two table sets, alternate frames)
    JSL FdVec_FFF7               the $0520 animation records (not analysed)
    Vblank_UnkA810               move every object, cull to the view, tick animations
    Field_ProcessAnimQueue       build queued sprite frames while there is time
    BRL Oam_BuildShadow          rebuild the OAM shadow for the next frame
  Field_WaitFrame ($C0:EC60)     handshake with the NMI
  BRA GameLoop_FrameBody

The Vblank_ names are historical: none of these routines runs inside the interrupt. Field_EndOfFrame's header says so plainly: it is "not an interrupt handler and waits for nothing itself". Two loops in this list stop on the PPU's V counter rather than a fixed count, so the work spreads over frames when there is a lot of it: the script runner (Vblank_ReadScanlineCounters) and the frame builder (Field_ProcessAnimQueue).

Field_EndOfFrameShort ($C0:00DE) runs only the two bank-$FD calls, for the fade and idle loops, and Field_IdleFrame ($C0:00EB) is one frame of upkeep without game logic: Field_FrameUpdate, Field_EndOfFrameShort, Field_WaitFrame.

docs.title: The handshake
docs.text: Field_WaitFrame ($C0:EC60, 23 bytes) counts Field_Unk58 up, increments Nmi_FramePending ($0152) and spins until it reads 0 again. Only NmiHandler clears it, after the frame's uploads (the "frame handshake" of ram_engine.inc). The NMI must be on, or Field_WaitFrame never returns.

docs.title: NmiHandler
docs.text:
NmiHandler ($C0:EA63, 509 bytes) is entered through the WRAM trampoline at $7E:0500 that InstallNMI writes. It saves A, X, Y, DP and DB, sets DB=$00, acknowledges the NMI (RDNMI), turns HDMA off and writes NMITIMEN and BGMODE. Then:

  • Lag frame (Nmi_FramePending = 0: the game has not reached its wait): no uploads at all.

  • Otherwise, with DP=$0100, the first that applies:

    1. Field_Unk47 nonzero: the first of its bits 0–3 that is set is cleared and its upload runs (Field_UploadUnk1D00, 1C00, 1F00, 57E0), one per frame; then the common uploads.
    2. A map redraw step in Field_MapRedrawDone: the 2 KB buffer Map_BufC800 to one of the map's tilemaps (Map_UploadBuf2K), or to VRAM $7000 / $7400; then Hdma_InitChannelsFD, skipping the common uploads.
    3. Otherwise one line of the staff credits if requested (Credits_UploadLine) and the Field_Unk36 upload if requested (Field_UploadUnk5800), then the common uploads.

    The common uploads are Pal_UploadCgram (the palette buffer at $7E:2200 to CGRAM), Oam_UploadShadow ($220 bytes from $0700 to OAM), VramQ_Flush (queued sprite tile uploads), then, with DP=$1D00, the map edge uploads for each layer and direction marked in Map_BuiltRowYInc … Map_BuiltColXDec (Map_UploadRowYInc1 … Map_UploadColXDec3, $C0:8445–$C0:87F0), Hdma_InitChannelsFD and Nmi_FramePending = 0. - Every NMI: JSL BankC2_Entry8002 (the joypad reader Menu_ReadPad), the window shadows Ppu_W12SelShadow … Ppu_CgwSelShadow to W12SEL … CGWSEL, the fixed colour, HDMAEN from Field_HdmaEnable and INIDISP from Fade_Brightness (forced blank when it is 0). These read the field bytes with absolute addresses, because on a lag frame DP is still the interrupted code's. Then it restores everything and returns with RTI.

The uploads use DMA channel 7. HDMA is set up by Hdma_InitChannelsFD ($FD:C1EE): eight indirect channels writing the BG tilemap bases, the three layers' scroll registers, the main and sub screens, two window positions and colour math, from one of two table sets in bank $7F ($7F:0F80 or $7F:1238).

docs.title: The field IRQ
docs.text:
IrqHandler ($C0:ECCC) is entered through the trampoline at $7E:0504 that InstallIRQ writes. It does nothing when Field_Unk0F bit 7 is set (who sets it is not traced) or when TIMEUP says this is not a timer IRQ. Otherwise it turns the V-count IRQ off until the next NMI, waits for H-blank, forces blank and turns HDMA off, then by Field_Unk53 bit 0, which EngFD_UnkC2C1 flips each frame, runs Irq_UploadTileAnim or FdVec_FFFD (bank $FD, not matched). The tile writes therefore happen every other frame.

Irq_UploadTileAnim ($C0:ED15) runs one queued tilemap job per call: either the new metatiles of a tile animation (the four tilemap words of each map tile, to the VRAM addresses a Mode*_Handler queued in TileAnim_VramAddrs) or DefaultHandler's single tile step. A step queued together with an animation waits for the next IRQ.

Before that, while Field_Unk63 is not negative, it calls Irq_DrawChoiceCursor ($C0:F05E). That routine draws a 2×2-tile picture (tiles $0FC–$0FF) at choice row Field_Unk63 (0–3) of the tilemap that Field_UploadUnk1C00 sends to VRAM $1C00, and puts Field_Unk2B78's grid entries back in the other three rows (Irq_ChoiceCursorClearRow0–3). A value of 4 or more clears all four rows and sets Field_Unk63 idle, so the next IRQs skip it. Its header calls this the choice cursor as "probable, not traced on screen": Field_Unk63 is the index Sub_1ADF steps with Up and Down while a message choice is active. What the four tiles show (the hand cursor, probably) and which layer uses the $1C00 tilemap are open in NEXT.md.

docs.title: The OAM shadow
docs.text: Oam_BuildShadow ($C0:B271) rebuilds the OAM shadow before the frame wait: low table at $0700, high table at $0900, split into three ranges that each object chooses with its Obj_OamFlags bits 2–3. It visits objects bucket by bucket, last bucket first (Obj_DrawBucket, 64 buckets; Obj_DrawLink puts an object in the bucket for its screen Y), calls Spr_AppendToOam for each, and parks every entry between a range's new end and last frame's end off screen (Y = $E0). The NMI copies the whole shadow to OAM. See How Sprite Init Works.

docs.title: Other frame cycles
docs.text:
• Scene mode (bank $C2). C2Scene_InstallInterrupts points the trampolines at C2Scene_NmiHandler ($C2:015E) and the one-byte C2Scene_IrqHandler (nothing in the scene code enables IRQs). Here the NMI does the frame's work itself: when C2Scene_NmiFlags bit 0 is set it uploads OAM, the palette (bit 1) and the PPU shadows, flushes the scene's VRAM queue, reads the joypad, then empties the sprite list, runs every task (C2Scene_TaskRunAll) and draws the list into the OAM shadow for the next NMI. The main loop only waits (C2Scene_WaitFrame: spin until C2Scene_FrameCounter changes) and dispatches on the scene mode. See Scene engine.
  • Menu (bank $C2). Menu_Nmi ($C2:840E) runs on its own stack with DP=$0D00; when the menu's threads have a frame ready it runs the upload (Menu_Unk85D6, not matched) and sets Menu_FrameReady to $FF. The thread scheduler Menu_RunThreads waits for that, runs each thread that is due until it yields, then clears the flag. Every NMI reads the pad and ticks the play-time clock (Menu_NmiPad). Menu_Irq is a bare RTI. See Menu.
  • Battle (bank $C1). BattleSys_PumpFrames ($C1:007E) sets Battle_FramePending and calls a bank-$CD vector until the flag is cleared. Its header reads this as a frame wait, but the clearing code in bank $CF is not traced, so "wait for the frame" is inferred, not proven.

docs.title: Menu (bank $C2)
docs.text:
The second half of bank $C2, from $C2:8000 on, is the menu. The field (Field_PauseAndMenuInput, Field_SceneChangeTick, Field_RunBankC2Mode5) and the scene mode's mode 5 call it with JSL BankC2_Entry8000 and an argument 0–6. Most of the menu's own screens are not matched yet, so this page covers the frame around them: the entry, the thread scheduler, the interrupt handlers and the helpers the screens share.

The menu runs with DP=$0000 and DB=$7E unless stated (names in include/ram_menu.inc and include/constants_menu.inc, prefix Menu).

See also: Scene engine, Frame cycle and NMI.

docs.title: Entry points
docs.text: Address Vector Goes to $C2:8000 BankC2_Entry8000 BankC2_MenuEntry, A = the argument (0–6) $C2:8002 BankC2_Entry8002 BankC2_ReadPadLong → Menu_ReadPad, the joypad reader $C2:8004 BankC2_Entry8004 BankC2_CommandLong → Menu_Unk8C36, A = a command (not matched)

docs.title: Entering and leaving
docs.text:
BankC2_MenuEntry ($C2:800E) turns interrupts off, saves DP, DB and P, keeps A and X (Menu_EntryArg, Menu_EntryX), forces blank and turns NMI, DMA and HDMA off.

  • Argument 0 on a new game (Menu_DataInitDone still 0): it fills the new game's data (Menu_InitNewGameData), clears two SRAM bytes and leaves through Menu_ExitRestart to GameLoop_Main. No menu is shown.
  • Otherwise: it moves the stack to Menu_StackTop, runs Menu_InitSystems, starts the play-time clock, picks the mode from Menu_EntryModes (arguments 0–6 give modes $0E, $00, $0C, $0D, $0F, $07, $0B), turns the NMI and interrupts on and hands over to Menu_RunThreads, which never returns.

Menu_InitSystems ($C2:8096) copies Menu_InterruptVectors ($C2:8406: JML Menu_Nmi, JML Menu_Irq) over the interrupt trampolines at $0500, sends five sound-driver commands ("meanings not traced"), sets up the PPU and clears RAM (Menu_InitPpuAndRam), builds the party lists (Menu_BuildPartyLists) and runs six more set-up routines that are not matched yet.

The menu leaves in one of two ways. Menu_Exit ($C2:82B2) frees every thread, fades out, restores the stack, P, DB and DP and returns with RTL to the caller of BankC2_Entry8000. Menu_ExitToGame ($C2:8320) fades out and jumps through ReentryVectors entry 0 to GameLoop_Main (the warm restart).

docs.title: The thread scheduler
docs.text:
The menu's screens run as up to eight cooperative threads. Menu_RunThreads ($C2:8190) keeps them in eight 8-byte slots (Menu_Thread, at $00B0), each with a 64-byte stack from $0A00 on. It starts Menu_MainThread in slot 1 and Menu_UnkE91B (not matched) in slot 3, then once a frame:

  1. waits until Menu_FrameReady is non-zero (the menu NMI has done its upload);
  2. for each slot in use, counts its .Wait down and runs the thread when it reaches 0: a new thread starts at its entry on a fresh stack, a waiting one gets its stack, X, Y, P and DP back and returns from its yield;
  3. after the last slot, clears Menu_FrameReady.

A thread gives the CPU back by jumping to one of three sub-entries:

Sub-entry What it does Menu_Yield ($C2:821E, JSR) Wait one frame Menu_YieldFrames ($C2:822B, JSR) Wait A frames (0 means 256) Menu_ThreadEnd ($C2:8216, JMP) Free the slot

Menu_StartThread ($C2:8249) puts a new thread in a slot (it starts on the next pass) and Menu_KillThreads ($C2:8255) frees the slots whose bits are set in A. Each thread also keeps one word, Menu_ThreadVar, across its yields. The header notes that DB is set only at the start of each frame, so a thread starts or resumes with the DB the thread before it left.

The main thread. Menu_MainThread ($C2:826C, slot 1) calls one handler a frame: entry Menu_ThreadVar of the current mode's list in Menu_ModeLists ($C2:8292, 16 modes). A handler moves on by changing Menu_ThreadVar or Menu_Mode. The mode lists themselves are not matched yet; modes 8–10 point at a bare RTS and are "probably not used".

docs.title: Interrupts and the frame
docs.text:
Menu_Nmi ($C2:840E) runs on its own stack with DP = Menu_NmiDp ($0D00). It counts frames, forces blank and, when the threads have a frame ready, turns HDMA off, runs the upload (Menu_Unk85D6, not matched) and sets Menu_FrameReady to $FF, which the scheduler waits for. Then it reads the pad and ticks the play-time clock (Menu_NmiPad, with the menu's auto-repeat: $20 frames before the first repeat, then 5), and sets the BG mode and the screen brightness. Menu_Irq ($C2:8472) is a bare RTI.

Menu_ReadPad ($C2:84D2) reads joypad 1 (Menu_PollPad), maps it through the configurable button map (Menu_MapButtons) and advances the play-time clock Menu_TickPlayTime ($C2:85AE: frames, seconds, two-digit minutes and hours, with a flag once it passes 99:59:59). The scene NMI and code in other banks call it too, the battle's play-time hit modifier among them.

docs.title: Shared helpers
docs.text:
• Set-up. Menu_InitPpuAndRam ($C2:940D) puts the PPU into the menu's starting state and clears VRAM and most of bank $7E with its DMA helpers; Menu_InitNewGameData fills the data of a new game (inferred from what it fills) and Menu_ClearConfigAndFlags clears the flag block, the play time and the settings, then loads the default settings and button map ($C2:956E–$C2:960A).
  • Fades. Menu_Fade ($C2:83D0) steps the brightness by A each frame, yielding between steps, until it reaches 0 or 15; Menu_FadeOut uses a step of −2, and Menu_StartFadeIn starts Menu_FadeInThread (+2 a frame) in slot 0.
  • VRAM queue. Menu_QueueVramRom / Menu_QueueVramWram ($C2:8385) append an 8-byte upload record from bank $C2 or $7E to Menu_VramQueue; Menu_FlushVramQueue ($C2:8663) sends them, newest first, with DMA channel 7 and empties the queue.
  • Palette and gradient. Menu_UploadPalette ($C2:86A9) sends the 512 bytes of Menu_PalBuf to CGRAM when Menu_PalDirty is set. Menu_BuildGradient ($C2:86DD) builds an HDMA table of colour-math lines for channel 0 in the buffer not built last, from Menu_GradSpec and the steps in Menu_GradientSteps.
  • Inventory. Menu_AddItem, Menu_RemoveItem and Menu_FindItem ($C2:8791–$C2:8815) add to and take from the 256 item slots, a count capped at 99.
  • Characters and party. Menu_BuildPartyLists lists the present characters and counts the active members (positions 0–2) and all of them; Menu_LoadCharRecA ($C2:8839) copies a character's $50-byte record to Menu_CurCharRec, and Menu_LoadPartyCharRec does it for the current member.
  • Items and equipment. Menu_ItemCategory ($C2:8881) sorts an item id into one of five categories by id range, and Menu_ItemDataPtrA / B give the address of its record in bank $CC ("what the records hold is not traced"). Menu_CountEquippedBy counts the characters that have an item equipped, and Menu_ListEquipItems ($C2:8953) lists the inventory items of one id range that Menu_Unk93A8 accepts (not matched; "probably 'the current character cannot equip it'" when it refuses).
  • Cursors and list arrows ($C2:89E4–$C2:8C35). Threads in slot 6 draw the blinking pointing-hand cursor sprites at the positions of Menu_CursorPos records, in four variants (Menu_StartCursorA–D; D shows one cursor per active party member). Menu_ListArrowsThread (slot 4) blinks the up and down arrows of a scrolling list: the up arrow when the list's top is not 0, the down arrow when it is below Menu_ListRows.

Quirks the headers keep include Menu_CursorStepD calling Menu_CursorPosAB with a 16-bit A, so its cursors sit one pixel lower than the others, and a missing CLC in Menu_ListArrowsThread that can put the down arrow one pixel lower.

docs.title: What is not matched yet
docs.text: From NEXT.md, in reach order: the command dispatcher Menu_Unk8C36 (behind BankC2_Entry8004, which calls the inventory routines), the set-up routines Menu_InitSystems calls, thread 3 (Menu_UnkE91B) and the mode handler lists. The menu NMI's upload Menu_Unk85D6 is also still open. After $C2:8C36 only the set-up at $C2:940D–$C2:960A and Menu_CursorRecOffset ($C2:EA27) are matched.

docs.title: Scene engine (bank $C2)
docs.text:
Bank $C2 holds a second, self-contained game mode that GameLoop_Main hands over to for locations $01F0 and up, and, from $C2:8000 on, the menu. This page calls it the scene mode, after its routines' C2Scene_ prefix; what the locations it runs show in the game is not traced yet, so the descriptions below stay with what the code does. Its text decoder has a page of its own: Text windows.

The scene mode has its own direct-page and low-WRAM layout (names in include/ram_menu.inc and include/constants_menu.inc, prefixes Menu, C2Scene and TextWin). It runs with DP=$0000 and DB=$00.

See also: Frame cycle and NMI, Architecture.

docs.title: Entry points
docs.text: Address Vector Goes to $C2:0000 BankC2_Entry0000 BankC2_SceneBoot (JML from GameLoop_Main for Loc_Id $01F0–$81EF) $C2:0003, $0006 BankC2_Entry0003/0006 TextWin_Init $C2:0009, $000C BankC2_Entry0009/000C TextWin_Step $C2:8000 BankC2_Entry8000 BankC2_MenuEntry, the menu $C2:8002 BankC2_Entry8002 Menu_ReadPad, the joypad reader every NMI calls $C2:8004 BankC2_Entry8004 Menu_Unk8C36, a command dispatcher (not matched)

docs.title: Boot and the main loop
docs.text:
BankC2_SceneBoot ($C2:000F) turns interrupts, NMI, DMA and HDMA off, sets forced blank and FastROM, writes the PPU registers (BankC2_InitHwRegs), clears the direct page, installs the scene's own interrupt handlers (C2Scene_InstallInterrupts), empties the VRAM queue and blacks out the palette, then jumps into C2Scene_Main ($C2:23A8).

C2Scene_Main clears VRAM, the tasks and the sprite list, places the start position and scroll from the field's entry tile, loads the scene (C2Scene_LoadScene), turns the NMI on and enters C2Scene_MainLoop, which waits a frame and dispatches on C2Scene_Mode through C2Scene_ModeTable ($C2:23DB, 10 words):

Mode Handler What it does 0, 1, 7 C2Scene_ModeIdle Send a pending sound command, nothing else 2 C2Scene_Mode2 Leave the scene: interrupts off, then JML to ReentryVectors, restarting the field's game loop (set by script op $05) 3 C2Scene_Mode3 Act on a C2Scene_ListA entry (probably an exit): start its script, or set up a location change and fall into mode 2 4 C2Scene_Mode4 Everything off, for good (probably waits for a reset) 5, 9 C2Scene_Mode5 Run the menu over the scene: save the scene, JSL BankC2_Entry8000, then rebuild it 6 C2Scene_Mode6 Run C2Scene_MapView (a BG mode 7 map of the scene; see Mode 6) between mosaic fades 8 C2Scene_Mode8 Run C2Scene_Dial (a BG mode 7 dial; see Mode 8) over a saved scene

The per-frame work is in the NMI, not the loop: C2Scene_NmiHandler ($C2:015E) uploads OAM, the palette and the PPU shadows, flushes the VRAM queue (C2Scene_VramQFlush), reads the joypad, then runs every task and rebuilds the sprite list for the next frame.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
The moving parts are tasks: 64 records of 64 bytes (C2Scene_Task at C2Scene_TaskRecords, $0B30) whose first word is a handler address. C2Scene_TaskRunAll ($C2:051D) calls every live handler once per frame; a handler that returns C=1 is done and its record is freed. C2Scene_TaskSpawn and C2Scene_TaskSpawnScript ($C2:048A–$C2:051C) start new ones, the Low variants in records 0–3 only. Motion is 16.16 fixed point (C2Scene_TaskMove), and positions wrap within the 1536 × 1024-pixel scene map (C2Scene_WrapTaskPos).

Matched task handlers include the screen fades and mosaics (C2Scene_TaskUnk20A2/2105/2194/ 21F8, started by script ops $28–$2B), the palette fade (C2Scene_TaskPalFade), the tile upload (C2Scene_TaskUnk1CF5), the sound zone task, and the tasks of the party and of two objects:

  • C2Scene_LeaderTask ($C2:3404 on): the first party member's sprite, walked with the D-pad in 8-pixel steps while BG1 and BG2 scroll with it; before each step it reads the property nibbles of the tiles ahead (C2Scene_GetTileProps) to block the step or set the trigger flags.
  • C2Scene_MemberTask ($C2:3AE2 on): the other party members, following with a route planner (C2Scene_MemberRoute, C2Scene_PathBlocked).
  • C2Scene_ObjATask and C2Scene_ObjBTask ($C2:42DD–$C2:5627): two objects the party can get into. Object A can rise, be steered with the D-pad and land again; its header says that what it is comes "from this behaviour only (a vehicle, probably)".
  • Two watchers, C2Scene_ObjWatch and C2Scene_TrigWatch ($C2:309E–$C2:3403): state machines that select an object when a button is held and the party's box overlaps it, or look the party's tile up in the trigger lists C2Scene_ListA–C.

None of the party tasks, objects or watchers has a reference in the bank's code; their headers say they are probably started from scene data.

docs.title: Scripts and animations
docs.text:
Tasks are driven by two byte-codes, both with the same handler convention (Z=0 with the bytes to advance in A, or Z=1 to stop for this frame and run the same op again):

  • Scene scripts: C2Scene_TaskRunScript ($C2:0F63) runs ops $00–$52 through C2Script_OpTable, all matched ($C2:0F63–$C2:1C83). They cover task and RAM bytes (set, clear, add, compare and branch), spawning scripts and tasks, calls and returns, waits, positions, velocities and animations, layer scrolls and redraws, VRAM queue entries, sound commands, the trigger lists, and C2Script_GoToLocation (op $05), which sets up a location change in the field's location block and selects mode 2. C2Scene_LoadScene starts the scene's first script on C2Scene_ScriptBuf ($7F:0400).
  • Animation scripts: C2Anim_Run ($C2:0E1D) runs a task's sprite script with eight ops (C2Anim_OpTable): clear, increment or decrement a task byte, jump back, show a frame for a number of frames, wait, queue a VRAM upload, end.

docs.title: Drawing
docs.text:
• BG layers. A layer's tilemap is built from 16×16 metatiles: a 96 × 64 metatile map per layer in bank $7E. C2Scene_DrawBgLayer ($C2:09C5) redraws the visible part of layer 1 or 2 column by column, sending each column to VRAM at once (so under forced blank or in vertical blank); C2Scene_Unk0568 / C2Scene_Unk066C ($C2:0568, $C2:066C) scroll a layer horizontally or vertically by a number of pixels and queue the new edge column or row.
  • Sprites. A doubly linked list of 64 16-byte nodes (C2Scene_SprNodes): every frame the NMI frees all nodes (C2Scene_SprResetLists), the tasks add what they show (C2Scene_SprAdd), and C2Scene_SprDrawList turns the list into OAM entries.
  • VRAM queue. 8-byte entries flushed by the NMI with DMA channel 0 (C2Scene_VramQFlush).

docs.title: Loading a scene
docs.text: Each scene has a header in bank $C6 (C2SceneRom_HeaderTable) whose bytes pick packed data from pack tables in the same bank; Decomp_ToWramVec unpacks each into WRAM. C2Scene_LoadScene ($C2:2C1D) loads the graphics and palettes into VRAM and CGRAM (C2Scene_LoadVram), then the metatiles, the maps, the tile-property pack at $7E:7000, the pack at $7E:7200 (it starts with a map of sound zones), the trigger lists, the script and two more packs, draws BG1 and BG2 and spawns the script task. What the packs hold is inferred from where they go. C2Scene_SaveState / C2Scene_RestoreState ($C2:2E23, $C2:2E72) copy the scene's state to bank $7F and back around the menu, and C2Scene_ReloadScene reloads its graphics.

docs.title: Screen effects
docs.text:
The scene scripts in bank $C3 call small routines in bank $C2 with op $34 and start task handlers with op $35 ($C2:754D–$C2:7B59 and $C2:7BC4–$C2:7DE3; none of them is referenced from bank $C2 code). They run inside C2Scene_TaskRunAll, from the scene NMI.

  • BG3 tasks: C2Scene_TaskBg3Drift moves layer 3 a pixel left every 4th frame and down every 8th; C2Scene_TaskBg3Slide and C2Scene_TaskBg3SlideFast move it at a fixed velocity; C2Scene_TaskBg3Wave bends it into a horizontal wave with HDMA (one sine period over 64 lines, repeated down the screen), and C2Scene_TaskBg3DriftWave drifts it as well. They wait while object A is in mode 8, and also scroll layer 3 by the leader's last move. C2Scene_TaskBg3LineWave (a wave on every odd line) and C2Scene_TaskBg1Pan (layer 1, a pixel every 4th frame) have no reference found.
  • Windows: C2Scene_Win1Init / Win1Step and C2Scene_Win2Init / Win2Step set up HDMA for window 1 or 2 and have BankC3_Entry0008 build the window table from the task's position and size into one of two buffers, so the table being written is not the one on screen ("the shape is not traced").
  • Line waves: C2Scene_Bg2HWaveInit / Bg2HWaveStep (and the unreferenced vertical pair) run a wave up layer 2: each step moves the lines up by one and adds a new bottom line from a sine. C2Scene_NoiseInit fills a line buffer with the first $1C0 bytes of ROM bank $C0 ("code, used as noise") and scrolls layers 1 and 2 by them; C2Scene_NoiseStep, NoiseShow and NoiseHide move through the noise, show it or hide it.
  • Placement and motion: random positions below the view or near fixed points, one of 16 random velocities, a gravity step (1/8 pixel a frame added to the Y velocity), a random nudge, and a test of whether the task is in view.
  • Other: clear, save and restore the party, unpack a BG pack, set or test flag bits, set the music byte Menu_Config1E, and C2Scene_BuildPatternTiles, ten tiles whose patterns get denser from pair to pair ("probably the steps of a dissolve").

The scene objects also use three direction helpers ($C2:2273–$C2:232C), with 256 steps per turn: C2Scene_Unk2273 and C2Scene_Unk2277 give the cosine and sine of a direction (from Rom_SineTable256, ±128 at the quarter turns), and C2Scene_Unk229D the direction from one point to another on the wrapping scene map. Their header suggests the names C2Scene_Cos256, C2Scene_Sin256 and C2Scene_DirToPoint.

docs.title: Mode 6: the map view
docs.text:
C2Scene_Mode6 ($C2:258D) fades out with a mosaic, turns interrupts, DMA and HDMA off, copies the direct page and the 64 task records to bank $7F and runs C2Scene_MapView ($C2:631F– $C2:6A33); afterwards it copies both back, reloads the graphics and fades in with a mosaic. The source names it a map view, "inferred from what it builds":

  • C2Scene_MapView sets BG mode 7, clears VRAM, the VRAM queue and the tasks, draws a label into sprite tiles (C2Scene_MapViewLabel, a string picked by Loc_Id $1F0–$1F7), sets up a blue fixed-colour gradient behind the picture with HDMA (C2Scene_MapViewGradient) and builds the picture (C2Scene_MapViewBuild).
  • The picture is a small map of the whole scene: C2Scene_MapDrawPixels draws the scene's two BG maps one pixel per metatile across and two down, 192 mode-7 tiles in all, uploaded a band at a time.
  • The task C2Scene_TaskMapZoom zooms out from the leader's position (C2Scene_StartX/Y) over 32 steps of the mode-7 matrix (C2Scene_MapZoomMatrix), then shows marker sprites for the leader, object A and the location (C2Scene_TaskLeaderMarker, C2Scene_TaskObjAMarker, C2Scene_TaskLocMarker). Pad bit 3 (C2Scene_MapViewExitBtn) zooms back in; at the end it sets mode 7, which ends C2Scene_MapView's wait.

docs.title: Mode 8: the dial
docs.text:
C2Scene_Mode8 ($C2:261D) fades out, sends sound command $82, saves the scene (C2Scene_SaveState) and runs C2Scene_Dial ($C2:6A34–$C2:754C). Afterwards it restores the scene and, unless two flag bytes at $7F:01F4/$7F:01F5 are set ("who sets them is not traced"), reloads the graphics and fades in; with them set it goes straight back to the loop in whatever mode the dial left.

The dial is a BG mode 7 screen whose per-line matrix is animated by C2Scene_TaskSwirl, with seven marker sprites (C2Scene_TaskDialMark) around a centre and a hand drawn with window 1, the fixed colour added inside it (C2Scene_DialDrawHand). Each marker stands for a location in C2Scene_DialLocs (or C2Scene_DialLocsLate, once a flag reaches C2Scene_DialLateFlag). C2Scene_TaskDial reads the pad: right or up (or one other button) turns the hand back a marker, left or down (or another button) forward one; confirming a marker that is not the current location stores its Loc_Id in C2Scene_ObjANextLoc and ends the dial, confirming the current one plays a sound ("probably a refusal sound"), and cancel stores C2Scene_DialNoDest and ends it.

docs.title: Menu side
docs.text: The menu in the second half of the bank has a page of its own: Menu.

docs.title: What is not matched yet
docs.text: Everything from $C2:0000 to the menu's start at $C2:8000 is matched, the $FF fill at $C2:7DE4 included. What is left in the bank is the menu's; see Menu.

docs.title: Sprites & objects
docs.text:
Field objects and how they reach the screen: the per-object animation tick and frame-build queue, the frame builders that copy graphics into a WRAM buffer and queue them for VRAM, and the OAM shadow that every visible object is appended to each frame. The full walk-through, with the data structures, is the Sprite Init Explainer.

The function table below lists the "Sprites & objects" group, the routines named Obj_*. The OAM and placement routines (Oam_*, Spr_*, SprBuf_*, VramQ_Flush) and Field_ProcessAnimQueue belong to the same system but are in the "Engine" group, on the Engine core page.

See also: Frame cycle and NMI, Field event scripts.

docs.title: Objects
docs.text:
Each location defines Evt_ObjCount objects (from its event data), kept in per-object tables indexed by object number × 2 (Obj_Cur, $016D). Positions (Obj_PosX/Y) are in 1/16 pixel, the high byte being the 16-pixel map tile; Obj_SprSize gives the size class (4, 8, 12 or 24 sprite tiles), Obj_State the progress of the frame build, Obj_OamFlags the OAM range.

Every frame, Vblank_UnkA810 ($C0:A810) walks the objects: moves each one (Obj_MoveStep, Obj_MoveStepFree), tests it against a window a little larger than the view (Obj_UpdateInView), and for one in the window ticks its animation (Obj_AnimTickAndQueue), works out its screen position (Obj_CalcScreenPos) and re-links it into the draw bucket for that position (Obj_DrawUnlink, Obj_DrawLink). Field_UnkB0E6 is the same pass at a location load, without movement.

docs.title: Frames
docs.text: When an object's animation timer runs out it joins the frame-build queue, and Field_ProcessAnimQueue builds queued frames while the frame still has time (Obj_BuildSpriteFrameStep → Obj_BuildFrame4 / 8 / 12, in one, two or three passes). A build copies the frame's 8×8 graphics tiles into one to three $200-byte chunks of the WRAM tile buffer at $7F:3800, queues them for VRAM, and writes the object's tile records. Spr_LoadLargeObj loads a 24-tile object in one go.

docs.title: Slots
docs.text: Objects take VRAM tile space and palette rows by kind (Obj_Unk1100): Obj_Unk6F9A / Obj_Unk7056 allocate and free tile slots (Obj_TileSlot), and Obj_Unk7170 / Obj_Unk72B4 / Obj_Unk734C palette slots (Obj_PalSlot; kinds 0–2 have fixed slots 5–7). These keep Unk names for their verified callers; NEXT.md suggests Obj_TileSlotAlloc/Free and Obj_PalSlotAlloc/AllocBtl/Free.

docs.title: Drawing
docs.text:
Oam_BuildShadow ($C0:B271) rebuilds the OAM shadow before each frame wait: for every object in every draw bucket, Spr_AppendToOam brings its tile records up to date (Spr_PrepareTiles) and copies them into one of three ranges of the shadow; leftover entries are parked off screen. The NMI uploads the shadow and the queued graphics.

docs.title: Text windows
docs.text:
The text decoder in bank $C2 ($C2:57DF–$C2:6262) turns a string of bytes into glyphs drawn pixel by pixel into a graphics buffer, a few characters per call. It is reached from other banks through two fixed vectors, so the field and the scene mode share it. All of it is matched, its tables included.

See also: Scene engine, Field event scripts.

docs.title: Calling it
docs.text:
Both entries work on a parameter block at $0200 (they set DP=$0200 themselves), which the caller fills first: the string number and string table, the output buffer, the mode, and before each step the number of characters to draw.

  • TextWin_Init ($C2:57DF, through BankC2_Entry0003) looks the string up in the table, sets state 0 and puts the pen at the left margin (or at 0 in some modes).
  • TextWin_Step ($C2:5823, through BankC2_Entry0009) draws one step: TextWin_CheckStatus runs the handler of the current status (TextWin_StatusTable, statuses $00–$20), which says whether to go on; if so, the handler of the current state runs.

Two callers use it. In the scene mode, the label task (C2Scene_LabelWait, C2Scene_LabelDraw) draws one character per frame. On the field, the message window step Field_Unk1F87 starts it with Field_MsgStart ($C0:20F2: the string from the treasure string table at $DE:FF00 for a treasure, else from the pointer Evt_OpB8_SetMsgPtr set; buffer $7E:F000, mode 0) and draws one glyph a step with Field_MsgStep ($C0:2126), acting on the status each step leaves: a new line, a new page, a timed wait, a wait ("for a press, probably") or the end. See Field event scripts.

docs.title: The string format
docs.text:
A string is a run of bytes at TextWin_TextPtr:

Bytes Meaning $A0–$FF A glyph, drawn by TextWin_DrawGlyph $21–$9F A dictionary entry (TextWin_DictPtrs, bank $DE): a sub-string of glyphs, drawn in state 1 $00–$20 A control code (TextWin_CodeTable, $C2:5903, 33 words)

The hex digit table TextWin_HexGlyphs gives "0"–"9" as $D4–$DD and "A"–"F" as $A0–$A5, so the banner reads $A0–$B9 as probably "A"–"Z" and $BA–$D3 as "a"–"z" (the names in ROM read as words that way).

The control codes matched include:

  • $01, $02 (TextWin_CodeWide): the next byte, with the code as its high byte, is a 16-bit glyph;
  • $00 and $04–$0C (TextWin_CodeSetStatus): set TextWin_Status to the code, which ends the step (0 is idle, "probably the end"; 5–12 reset the pen); $03 does the same after storing an argument byte;
  • $0D, $0E, $0F (TextWin_CodeNum8/16/24): a number in decimal (3, 5 or 8 digits, leading zeros trimmed) or in hex, drawn in states 2 and 3;
  • $11, $13–$1E, $20: names: the characters' names kept in bank $7E ($13–$1A, $20, and $11 with an argument), the party members by position ($1B–$1D, TextWin_CodeMemberName), and a fixed "Nadia" string ($1E, TextWin_CodeNadia);
  • $12 $00 / $12 $01 (TextWin_ExtTechName, TextWin_ExtEnemyName): a tech or enemy name from the ROM name tables;
  • $1F (TextWin_CodeItemName): the name of the item in Treasure_ItemId.

docs.title: The states
docs.text:
State Handler Draws 0 TextWin_State0 ($C2:58B2) Glyphs from the string; starts dictionary entries and control codes 1 TextWin_State1 ($C2:5BF5) A sub-string: a dictionary entry or a name 2 TextWin_State2 ($C2:5C3E) Number digits 3 TextWin_State3 ($C2:5C77) Number digits

Each glyph drawn uses up one of TextWin_StepCount; when it runs out the step ends with TextWin_StatusStepDone, and the next step goes on in the same state. Each of states 1–3 leaves through a small exit table chosen by what is left of the sub-string and of the step.

docs.title: Drawing a glyph
docs.text:
TextWin_DrawGlyph ($C2:5DC4) reads the glyph's 24 bytes from the font in bank $FF, shifts them to the pen's pixel position within its 8-pixel tile column, and ORs them into the output buffer: TextWin_Blit2bpp or TextWin_Blit4bpp by the mode, each with a table of eight shift entry points. The pen then moves on by the glyph's width from TextWin_GlyphWidths (96 entries, one per glyph $A0–$FF), so the font is proportional.

Numbers go through TextWin_Dec8, TextWin_Dec16 and TextWin_Dec24 ($C2:615E–$C2:6230), which divide by powers of ten with shift-and-subtract loops (TextWin_DivBits, TextWin_Div24Bits), and TextWin_HexByte for hex.

docs.title: Quirks kept
docs.text: TextWin_DrawGlyph indexes the width table with the glyph's low byte only, so a 16-bit glyph from codes $01/$02 with a low byte under $A0 reads past the table. TextWin_StateTable's verified header still calls its handlers unmatched; NEXT.md lists it as a stale header to fix at its next edit.
